# DeployEx

> DeployEx deploys and runs BEAM applications (Elixir, Erlang, Gleam) from their release package. It performs a full deployment or a hot upgrade depending on the release's content, and uses OTP distribution to monitor and operate the applications it runs. It runs as a service on a host or inside a container, including Kubernetes.

DeployEx is not a build tool and does not replace a CI/CD pipeline. A separate pipeline builds the release package; DeployEx picks it up from release storage (S3, GCS, or a local path) and runs it. It is distributed as a GitHub release (host binaries), not as a Hex package; a Dockerfile is provided to build your own container image, not a published one.

Current status: pre-1.0, see the version badge in [README.md](https://github.com/deployex/deployex/blob/main/README.md). The [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/deployex/deployex/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) lists every merged pull request per release.

## Start here

- [README](https://github.com/deployex/deployex/blob/main/README.md): what DeployEx is, host vs container, where to start
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/deployex/deployex/blob/main/AGENTS.md): umbrella app structure, dev commands, and what an AI coding agent may run without asking first - read this before making code changes to DeployEx itself
- [YAML configuration](https://github.com/deployex/deployex/blob/main/guides/docs/yaml/README.md): every `deployex.yaml` key, including the release and secrets adapters and their options
- [Agent API](https://github.com/deployex/deployex/blob/main/guides/docs/agent-api/README.md): a scoped JSON API and an event stream (Phoenix Channels) to read host/app state, logs, and operate (restart, clear ghosted versions, set mode) without the dashboard - the one DeployEx surface meant to be driven by a script or another agent, not a human

## Running it

- [Docker and Kubernetes](https://github.com/deployex/deployex/blob/main/guides/docs/docker/README.md): one container with Docker Compose, one pod on a local `kind` cluster, and several pods - what was measured in each setup and what is still open (there is no Helm chart or operator yet; the Kubernetes manifests are hand-written and meant as a starting point, not a packaged install)
- [Hot upgrades](https://github.com/deployex/deployex/blob/main/guides/docs/hot-upgrades/README.md): when a release can be applied without restarting the BEAM node, and what it leaves to the application
- Local, no cloud dependency: [Elixir](https://github.com/deployex/deployex/blob/main/guides/docs/local-elixir/README.md), [Elixir with Ecto](https://github.com/deployex/deployex/blob/main/guides/docs/local-elixir-ecto/README.md), [Elixir umbrella](https://github.com/deployex/deployex/blob/main/guides/docs/local-elixir-umbrella/README.md), [Erlang](https://github.com/deployex/deployex/blob/main/guides/docs/local-erlang/README.md), [Gleam](https://github.com/deployex/deployex/blob/main/guides/docs/local-gleam/README.md)

## Cloud guides (DeployEx as a host service)

- AWS, with Terraform: [Elixir](https://github.com/deployex/deployex/blob/main/guides/docs/aws-elixir/README.md), [Elixir with a DB certificate](https://github.com/deployex/deployex/blob/main/guides/docs/aws-elixir-db-certificate/README.md), [Erlang](https://github.com/deployex/deployex/blob/main/guides/docs/aws-erlang/README.md), [Gleam](https://github.com/deployex/deployex/blob/main/guides/docs/aws-gleam/README.md), [air-gapped](https://github.com/deployex/deployex/blob/main/guides/docs/aws-air-gapped/README.md)
- GCP, with Terraform: [Elixir](https://github.com/deployex/deployex/blob/main/guides/docs/gcp-elixir/README.md)
